name_reason: Compliant data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> global name. Domain 'input' matches home input.c and the sole game writer fd2_wait_for_input_with_idle. Descriptor accurately conveys: 'idle' (the idle-poll loop), 'current_bios_tick' (the freshly-snapshotted BIOS 0:046C 18.2 Hz tick), 'word' (reflects the uint16 / word datatype, store is MOV [0x539F0],AX). No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix matching 0x539F0). Name reflects both purpose and data type per convention.
purpose: Write-only snapshot latch holding the most recent BIOS midnight-tick (0:046C, 18.2 Hz word) value captured each idle iteration of fd2_wait_for_input_with_idle.
logic_summary: In fd2_wait_for_input_with_idle's idle-poll loop, each pass reads the BIOS tick word at 0:046C into AX and stores it here (MOV [0x539F0],AX @ 0x11AC9). The cursor-blink redraw decision then compares the freshly-read tick still held in the register (MOVSX EDX,AX @ 0x11ACF) against the sibling data_fd2_input_idle_last_rendered_tick_word @ 0x539F2 -- NOT a re-read of this word. Thus 0x539F0 is a stored snapshot only; it is never read at runtime (zero read-xrefs). The redraw cadence is ~18.2 Hz, producing the cursor-blink animation.
element_semantics: Low 16 bits of the BIOS midnight-tick counter at segment 0:0x46C (~18.2 Hz). Scalar, not an array.
comment_original_issue: Original src comment said the value was 'Compared against the last-rendered tick to drive the redraw', which overstates this global's role: 0x539F0 itself is never read (write-only latch); the compare uses the register-held freshly-read tick vs sibling 0x539F2. Refined to state write-only / no runtime readers and that the compare is register-vs-0x539F2.
notes: Memory at 0x539F0 reads all-zero, consistent with BSS zero-init. Writers per get_xrefs_to: fd2_wait_for_input_with_idle (game, WRITE @ 0x11AC9) + _cstart_/crt_equivalent_dos_main_bootstrap (BSS zero-init, WRITE @ 0x3CB65/0x3CB6C); no game writer mutates it after the per-iteration snapshot. is_const=false because there is a game-side write (the per-iteration snapshot store). globals.h declaration (uint16, /* 0x539F0 */) is correct. Disassembly of fd2_wait_for_input_with_idle confirms 16-bit store width (word) and write-only access pattern. Only name/comment touched; no logic changed.
